track: finite-size / boundary-condition convergence of the s_d = 0.01 crossover (T8 cluster 1 + walled-boundary cluster)
question: Does the crossover load theta* = U_d*/s_d at s_d = 0.01 drift with lattice size L, or plateau? And does a walled transverse boundary shift theta* outside the periodic interval?

reference_protocol_matched.source_pool: ridge_profile_analysis_pool.parquet (round-7 primary pool; 12,756 loaded + 2,856 neutral, 192x32, sd rungs 0.0025..0.04)
reference_protocol_matched.reference_geometry: L_long = 192, L_short = 32, Moore stencil, periodic transverse boundary
reference_protocol_matched.kernel: evolution_strip.py from round-8/9 kernel bundle (artifact 382c3b90), unmodified; helper evolution_fast4.py

fixed_parameters.initial_condition: clone A x <= L_long/2, clone B the rest, all fitness 1.0 (no burn-in)
fixed_parameters.fixation_criterion: exact frame at which cntA == 0 or cntB == 0 (early stop); t_fix = -1 if frame cap reached (censored)

reference_protocol_matched.load_axis: theta = U_d/s_d = mud/sd (deposited convention); loaded arms use sd = 0.01, mud = theta * 0.01
reference_protocol_matched.pool_run_counts_at_sd_0.01: 96-246 loaded runs per theta rung (14 rungs), pooled 2,856-run neutral anchor
reference_protocol_matched.estimator: median T_fix(theta) / median T_fix(own neutral anchor) ratio; crossing located by linear interpolation of the RATIO against log(theta) at the first descending crossing (deposited 'loglin' scheme); level 1/2 = legacy convention

design.walled_arm: W32 (192x32, periodic_y = False; x walled as always)

W32.boundary: WALLED transverse (non-periodic y; x always walled)

seeds.policy: one contiguous fresh block per cell, disjoint per cell and per arm; ledger maximum before this campaign = 13,777,699 (round-9 advantaged-competitor), sibling round-10 tracks running concurrently reserve 13,780,000-13,819,999 (low-s_d campaign) and 13,800,000-13,803,999 (ridge-exponent campaign) and use 13,900,000+ smoke seeds; this campaign therefore allocates strictly ABOVE all of them
seeds.layout: cell base + rung_index*200 + rep for loaded rungs (rep < n_per_rung <= 200); anchors at base + 3000 + rep
seeds.overlap_with_deposited_tables: verified 0 seeds of 22,130 fall inside any deposited per-run table's seed range (audit in fss_summary.json)

deviations_declared_in_advance: G768 runs 150 (not 200) loaded runs per rung and a 250-run anchor; G1536 runs a reduced 10-rung ladder (theta 0.2..10, dropping 0.05/0.1/0.15/1.2) at 48 runs per rung with a 100-run anchor. Both reductions are compute-driven (G1536 dominates the budget at ~0.9 core-hour per neutral run); the design keeps the largest lattice at reduced replication rather than dropping it, and the memo will report its wider bootstrap intervals as such.

Frame cap (numgen) is a censoring bound only and does not enter the dynamics. It is kept at the pool's 2e7 for all cells with L_long <= 384 and both L_short arms and the walled arm, raised to 4e7 for G768 and 1e8 for G1536 so that neutral anchors do not censor (the deposited 768x32 finite-size ensemble at cap 4e7 had zero censoring). Any censored run is reported and handled by Kaplan-Meier-consistent median (median unaffected if fewer than half censored).

Sibling round-10 campaigns share the 64-core host during the launch window; worker count is set to the free capacity at launch time and may vary across waves. This affects only wall time, never the RNG stream (each run is single-threaded and seeded per run).

per_cell_crossover.half_drop_estimator: convention-free primary: the two plateaus are estimated as the mean of log median T_fix over the two smallest thetas measured in the cell (upper plateau, theta 0.05 & 0.1; for G1536 theta 0.2 & 0.3) and over the two largest (lower plateau, theta 5 & 10); theta_half = the load at which log median T_fix crosses the midpoint of the two plateau levels, by linear interpolation of log-median vs log-theta at the first descending crossing. Reported as [value, ci_lo, ci_hi].
per_cell_crossover.legacy_level_half: deposited convention: ratio R(theta) = median T_fix(theta)/median T_fix(own anchor); crossing of R = 1/2 by linear interpolation of R against log(theta) at the first descending crossing (loglin scheme); isotonic (weighted PAVA) variant reported as a sensitivity column.
per_cell_crossover.additional_levels: R = 0.4 and R = 0.6 crossings reported for the convention-envelope
per_cell_crossover.bootstrap: run-level, B = 2000 resamples per cell; every loaded rung AND the cell's own anchor resampled with replacement within each replicate; CIs are the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles of the replicate distribution

convergence_test.ladder: the five L_long values at L_short = 32 (96, 192, 384, 768, 1536)

fits.constant: theta*(L) = theta_inf (weighted least squares in log theta*, weights = 1/bootstrap variance)
fits.power_law_plus_plateau: theta*(L) = theta_inf + A * L^(-b), b > 0 (weighted nonlinear least squares in log theta*)

convergence_test.comparison: AICc difference (n = 5, k = 1 vs 3) and an F-test of the nested improvement; the fit-family bootstrap re-fits both models on each of >= 2000 run-level bootstrap replicates of the five theta*(L) values to give the interval of theta_inf and of the extrapolated large-L limit; monotone drift is additionally tested by a Spearman-type sign test on the bootstrap replicates (P(all four successive differences same sign))
convergence_test.verdict_rule: PLATEAU if (i) the constant model is preferred by dAICc and (ii) |theta*(1536) - theta*(96)| is smaller than the summed half-widths of their CIs; DRIFT if the power-law-plus-plateau is preferred AND the bootstrap sign test supports monotone change; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. The same test is repeated on the half-drop and the level-1/2 estimators; if they disagree the memo reports both.
convergence_test.L_short_axis: S16, G192, S64 at fixed L_long = 192 test whether theta* moves with the transverse size at fixed longitudinal size (three-point weighted slope of theta* vs log L_short with bootstrap CI)

analysis_plan_preregistered.walled_test: theta*_W32 minus theta*_G192 (paired estimator, joint bootstrap over both cells' runs); walled arm 'shifts theta*' if the 95% CI of the difference excludes 0, and it is separately reported whether theta*_W32 lies outside the G192 95% CI (the reviewer's stated criterion). Also compared against the deposited pool's own 192x32 crossing.
analysis_plan_preregistered.pool_replication_check: G192 (fresh seeds, identical protocol) vs the deposited sd=0.01 pool: level-1/2 crossing must agree within joint bootstrap CI; rung-wise Mann-Whitney and Fisher-combined p reported (pool consistency, as in round 7).
analysis_plan_preregistered.reporting_discipline: every reported number is a field in fss_summary.json; all estimates stored as [value, ci_lo, ci_hi] from >= 2000 run-level bootstrap resamples

compute.host: 64-core local, shared with two sibling campaigns at launch
compute.workers: free capacity at launch, up to 60
compute.task_order: largest lattices and neutral anchors first (long-tail first)

deviations_executed_during_run.when: 2026-07-18 ~21:50 UTC, after all six small/medium cells had completed (19,200 runs) and 100 large-lattice neutral anchors had landed
deviations_executed_during_run.what: G768 loaded arm reduced 150 -> 60 runs per rung (14 rungs) and anchor 250 -> 100; G1536 loaded arm reduced 48 -> 24 runs per rung (10 rungs) and anchor 100 -> 60. Truncation keeps the LOWEST seed indices of each pre-allocated rung/anchor block (task list fss_tasks_reduced.json), i.e. a prefix of the pre-registered list, not a selection on outcomes; no loaded large-lattice run had been observed at the time. Runs already banked beyond the reduced anchor counts are retained as extra data.
deviations_executed_during_run.why: the remaining large-lattice work at the pre-registered replication (about 190 core-hours at the solo per-site-frame rate) could not be completed within the session at the observed throughput: concurrent sibling campaigns on the shared 64-core host inflated the per-site-frame cost by a factor of about 1.8-2.4 (measured 3.4-4.8e-9 s vs 1.85e-9 s solo), i.e. an estimated ~340-450 core-hours (~6+ h wall) still to go. NOTE (correction to the first-written version of this record): the observed neutral anchor medians (G768 5.1e6, G1536 1.4e7 frames) are BELOW the design cost model's per-run assumptions (neut[768]=7,258,605.5 taken from the deposited prior 768x32 finite-size ensemble; neut[1536]=7,258,605.5*2**1.7253~2.40e7), not above them; the overrun is a host-contention throughput shortfall against the pre-registered run counts, not a mis-estimated neutral fixation time. The design's stated rule is to run the largest lattices at reduced replication rather than drop them; the ladder stays complete (5 L_long points) and the reduced counts (60/rung + 100 anchor at 768; 24/rung + 60 anchor at 1536) still meet or exceed the deposited prior finite-size ensemble (60 neutral runs at 768x32).
deviations_executed_during_run.consequence: wider bootstrap intervals on the two largest lattices; reported as such in the memo. Frame caps unchanged (G768 4e7, G1536 1e8; observed max anchor t_fix 1.3e7 and 5.1e7 respectively, no censoring).

deviations_executed_during_run.when: 2026-07-19 ~00:00 UTC, after 11 G1536 loaded runs and 49-58 large-lattice anchors had completed (no loaded-ladder result observed)
deviations_executed_during_run.what: G1536 loaded arm reduced again, 24 -> 12 runs per rung (all 10 rungs kept); G1536 anchor stays at 60. Same prefix-truncation rule (lowest 12 seed indices per rung; fss_tasks_reduced2.json). G768 unchanged from the first reduction (60/rung + 100 anchor).
deviations_executed_during_run.why: sustained host contention (load average ~95 on 64 cores from concurrent sibling campaigns) held the G1536 loaded ladder to ~30 completions/hour, implying ~7 more hours for the first-reduced 240-run ladder. Rule as before: keep the largest lattice at reduced replication rather than drop it.
deviations_executed_during_run.consequence: the 1536x32 point carries the widest bootstrap interval of the ladder (12 runs per rung); the convergence fit weights it by 1/variance accordingly, and the memo flags it as the least-replicated point.
